1344.title: 18 U.S.C. 1344, bank fraud

rows.trigger: Knowingly executing, or attempting to execute, a scheme or artifice to defraud a financial institution. Independent route to the penalty; the statute joins paragraphs (1) and (2) with "or", so this prong alone supports conviction. No value or quantity element anywhere in the section, so there is no lower bound and no upper bound. Punishment: fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both. The $1,000,000 figure is a fine ceiling, not a trigger threshold. No "except as provided in" clause appears in this section.
rows.quote: Whoever knowingly executes, or attempts to execute, a scheme or artifice- ... (1) to defraud a financial institution; or ... shall be fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Knowingly executing, or attempting to execute, a scheme or artifice to obtain money, funds, credits, assets, securities, or other property owned by, or under the custody or control of, a financial institution by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises. Independent route to the same penalty; not an additional element that must be proven alongside paragraph (1). No dollar amount or quantity is an element, so there is no lower bound and no upper bound. Punishment: fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both. The $1,000,000 figure is a fine ceiling, not a trigger threshold. No "except as provided in" clause appears in this section.
rows.quote: Whoever knowingly executes, or attempts to execute, a scheme or artifice- ... (2) to obtain any of the moneys, funds, credits, assets, securities, or other property owned by, or under the custody or control of, a financial institution, by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises; ... shall be fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both.

1343.title: Fraud by wire, radio, or television

rows.trigger: Base offense. NO LOWER BOUND: the statute states no dollar amount, quantity, or value element of any kind; liability attaches to any covered transmission regardless of amount, and no upper bound is stated either. Elements: having devised or intending to devise a scheme or artifice to defraud, or for obtaining money or property by false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises, and transmitting or causing to be transmitted by wire, radio, or television communication in interstate or foreign commerce any writings, signs, signals, pictures, or sounds for the purpose of executing the scheme. Penalty: imprisonment not more than 20 years, or a fine under this title, or both. The fine is a penalty cap set by cross-reference to this title and is not a trigger threshold.
rows.quote: Whoever, having devised or intending to devise any scheme or artifice to defraud, or for obtaining money or property by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises, transmits or causes to be transmitted by means of wire, radio, or television communication in interstate or foreign commerce, any writings, signs, signals, pictures, or sounds for the purpose of executing such scheme or artifice, shall be fined under this title or imprisoned not more than 20 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Enhancement, second sentence, financial-institution branch. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar or quantity threshold; the trigger is solely that the violation affects a financial institution, at any amount. Penalty raised to imprisonment not more than 30 years, or a fine not more than $1,000,000, or both. The $1,000,000 figure is a fine ceiling, a penalty cap, not a trigger threshold, so it is recorded here and in the quote and never in min or max.
rows.quote: If the violation ... affects a financial institution, such person shall be fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both.

rows.trigger: Enhancement, second sentence, disaster/emergency branch. NO LOWER BOUND: no dollar or quantity threshold; the trigger is solely that the violation occurs in relation to, or involves any benefit authorized, transported, transmitted, transferred, disbursed, or paid in connection with, a presidentially declared major disaster or emergency as defined in section 102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5122), at any amount. Penalty raised to imprisonment not more than 30 years, or a fine not more than $1,000,000, or both. The $1,000,000 figure is a fine ceiling, a penalty cap, not a trigger threshold, so it is recorded here and in the quote and never in min or max.
rows.quote: If the violation occurs in relation to, or involving any benefit authorized, transported, transmitted, transferred, disbursed, or paid in connection with, a presidentially declared major disaster or emergency (as those terms are defined in section 102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5122)), ... such person shall be fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both.

2251.title: Sexual exploitation of children

rows.trigger: Production offense. Employing, using, persuading, inducing, enticing, or coercing a minor to engage in, or having a minor assist another to engage in, or transporting a minor in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce with intent that the minor engage in, sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing a visual depiction or transmitting a live visual depiction. No dollar or quantity threshold; value is not an element, so min and max are null. Punishment is assigned only by cross-reference to subsection (e): imprisonment not less than 15 years nor more than 30 years, escalating to 25-50 years with one qualifying prior and 35 years to life with 2 or more qualifying priors. No 'except as provided in' clause appears anywhere in this section.
rows.quote: Any person who employs, uses, persuades, induces, entices, or coerces any minor to engage in, or who has a minor assist any other person to engage in, or who transports any minor in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce, or in any Territory or Possession of the United States, with the intent that such minor engage in, any sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing any visual depiction of such conduct or for the purpose of transmitting a live visual depiction of such conduct, shall be punished as provided under subsection (e), if such person knows or has reason to know that such visual depiction will be transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed, if that visual depiction was produced or transmitted using materials that have been mailed, shipped, or transported in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means, including by computer, or if such visual depiction has actually been transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed.

rows.trigger: Parent, legal guardian, or person having custody or control of a minor who knowingly permits the minor to engage in, or to assist another to engage in, sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing a visual depiction or transmitting a live visual depiction. No dollar or quantity threshold; min and max null. Punishment assigned only by cross-reference to subsection (e): 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years with one qualifying prior, 35 years to life with 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any parent, legal guardian, or person having custody or control of a minor who knowingly permits such minor to engage in, or to assist any other person to engage in, sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing any visual depiction of such conduct or for the purpose of transmitting a live visual depiction of such conduct shall be punished as provided under subsection (e) of this section, if such parent, legal guardian, or person knows or has reason to know that such visual depiction will be transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed, if that visual depiction was produced or transmitted using materials that have been mailed, shipped, or transported in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means, including by computer, or if such visual depiction has actually been transported or transmitted using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed.

rows.trigger: Extraterritorial production. Same production conduct as (a) but committed outside of the United States, its territories or possessions, in a circumstance described in paragraph (2). No dollar or quantity threshold; min and max null. Punishment assigned only by cross-reference to subsection (e): 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years with one qualifying prior, 35 years to life with 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any person who, in a circumstance described in paragraph (2), employs, uses, persuades, induces, entices, or coerces any minor to engage in, or who has a minor assist any other person to engage in, any sexually explicit conduct outside of the United States, its territories or possessions, for the purpose of producing any visual depiction of such conduct, shall be punished as provided under subsection (e).

rows.trigger: Jurisdictional circumstance element for (c)(1); assigns no punishment of its own and carries no value or quantity threshold, so min and max are null. Both subparagraphs read in full: (A) intent that the depiction be transported to the United States, or (B) actual transport of the depiction to the United States. Either alternative suffices; neither states any lower or upper bound.
rows.quote: The circumstance referred to in paragraph (1) is that- (A) the person intends such visual depiction to be transported to the United States, its territories or possessions, by any means, including by using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or mail; or (B) the person transports such visual depiction to the United States, its territories or possessions, by any means, including by using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or mail.

rows.trigger: Advertising offense. Knowingly making, printing, or publishing, or causing to be made, printed, or published, any notice or advertisement seeking or offering either (A) to receive, exchange, buy, produce, display, distribute, or reproduce a visual depiction whose production involves a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct, or (B) participation in any act of sexually explicit conduct by or with any minor for the purpose of producing a visual depiction. Both subparagraphs read; neither states a dollar, quantity, or count threshold, so min and max are null. Punishment assigned only by cross-reference to subsection (e): 15 to 30 years, 25 to 50 years with one qualifying prior, 35 years to life with 2 or more qualifying priors.
rows.quote: Any person who, in a circumstance described in paragraph (2), knowingly makes, prints, or publishes, or causes to be made, printed, or published, any notice or advertisement seeking or offering- (A) to receive, exchange, buy, produce, display, distribute, or reproduce, any visual depiction, if the production of such visual depiction involves the use of a minor engaging in sexually explicit conduct and such visual depiction is of such conduct; or (B) participation in any act of sexually explicit conduct by or with any minor for the purpose of producing a visual depiction of such conduct; shall be punished as provided under subsection (e).

rows.trigger: Jurisdictional circumstance element for (d)(1); assigns no punishment of its own and carries no value or quantity threshold, so min and max are null. Both subparagraphs read in full: (A) knowledge or reason to know that the notice or advertisement will be transported in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce or mailed, or (B) the notice or advertisement is actually so transported or mailed.
rows.quote: The circumstance referred to in paragraph (1) is that- (A) such person knows or has reason to know that such notice or advertisement will be transported using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means including by computer or mailed; or (B) such notice or advertisement is transported using any means or facility of interstate or foreign commerce or in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce by any means including by computer or mailed.

rows.trigger: Base penalty for an individual who violates this section, with no qualifying prior conviction: fine under title 18 plus imprisonment of not less than 15 years and not more than 30 years. The 15-year floor is a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment, not a value threshold, and the 30-year ceiling is a term of imprisonment, not a value threshold; the fine is a penalty cap, never a trigger. min and max are therefore null.
rows.quote: Any individual who violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 15 years nor more than 30 years...

rows.trigger: Attempt and conspiracy are punished identically to the completed offense. The phrase 'or attempts or conspires to violate' sits inside the same sentence that sets the individual penalty, so an attempt or conspiracy carries the same 15-year mandatory minimum and 30-year maximum, and the same escalation to 25-50 years and 35 years to life on priors. The parallel organization sentence likewise reaches attempts and conspiracies. No separate or reduced range is stated for inchoate conduct, and no dollar or quantity threshold applies, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: Any individual who violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 15 years nor more than 30 years... Any organization that violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title.

rows.trigger: Enhanced range on ONE prior conviction: imprisonment not less than 25 years nor more than 50 years, plus a fine. The qualifying prior may be under chapter 110 of title 18 ('this chapter'), section 1591, chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117, or under the Uniform Code of Military Justice, or under the laws of any State relating to aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse, abusive sexual contact involving a minor or ward, or sex trafficking of children, or the production, possession, receipt, mailing, sale, distribution, shipment, or transportation of child pornography. Note that section 1591 and the child-pornography-conduct clause appear in this one-prior list but NOT in the two-or-more-prior list. Terms of years are not value thresholds and the fine is a penalty cap, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: ...but if such person has one prior conviction under this chapter, section 1591, chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117, or under the Uniform Code of Military Justice or the laws of any State relating to aggravated sexual abuse, sexual abuse, abusive sexual contact involving a minor or ward, or sex trafficking of children, or the production, possession, receipt, mailing, sale, distribution, shipment, or transportation of child pornography, such person shall be fined under this title and imprisoned for not less than 25 years nor more than 50 years...

rows.trigger: Enhanced range on 2 OR MORE prior convictions: imprisonment not less than 35 years nor more than life, plus a fine. This list is narrower than the one-prior list: chapter 110 of title 18 ('this chapter'), chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117, or the Uniform Code of Military Justice, or the laws of any State relating to the sexual exploitation of children. Section 1591 does not appear here, and the itemized child-pornography-conduct clause is replaced by 'relating to the sexual exploitation of children'. The upper term is life, which is the stated ceiling of the sentence, not a value threshold; there is no dollar or quantity element, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: ...but if such person has 2 or more prior convictions under this chapter, chapter 71, chapter 109A, or chapter 117, or under the Uniform Code of Military Justice or the laws of any State relating to the sexual exploitation of children, such person shall be fined under this title and imprisoned not less than 35 years nor more than life.

rows.trigger: Organizational defendant: an organization that violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section is punished by fine under title 18 only. No term of imprisonment is stated for an organization and no mandatory minimum applies to it. The fine is a penalty, never a trigger, so min and max are null.
rows.quote: Any organization that violates, or attempts or conspires to violate, this section shall be fined under this title.

rows.trigger: Death-results enhancement: whoever, in the course of an offense under this section, engages in conduct resulting in the death of a person is punished by death, or by imprisonment for not less than 30 years, or for life. The 30-year floor is a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment and there is no stated numeric upper bound other than life; the statute states no dollar or quantity element, so min and max are null. This sentence applies to 'Whoever' and is not limited to individuals or to defendants with priors.
rows.quote: Whoever, in the course of an offense under this section, engages in conduct that results in the death of a person, shall be punished by death or imprisoned for not less than 30 years or for life.

1344.notes:
INDEPENDENT FETCH: curl of the OLRC page yields exactly four operative text units inside field-start:statute -- (a) flush intro "Whoever knowingly executes, or attempts to execute, a scheme or artifice-", (b) "(1) to defraud a financial institution; or", (c) "(2) to obtain any of the moneys, funds, credits, assets, securities, or other property owned by, or under the custody or control of, a financial institution, by means of false or fraudulent pretenses, representations, or promises;", (d) flush penalty "shall be fined not more than $1,000,000 or imprisoned not more than 30 years, or both." I also enumerated every field marker in the raw HTML: cite, expcite, head, statute, sourcecredit, notes (containing only a miscellaneous-note that is the bare heading "Editorial Notes", and one amendment-note with the 1990 and 1989 entries). There is no additional penalty, mandatory minimum, enhancement, or definitional provision anywhere in the section.

1. MISSING PROVISIONS -- none. My independent walk produces exactly two punishable prongs, (1) and (2), each reachable independently through the single flush penalty clause. Both have rows. The flush penalty clause is not a separate offense and is correctly attributed to both rows rather than given a phantom row of its own. No paragraph or subparagraph lacks a row. No no-lower-bound trap exists here to be missed, because the section has no tiered subparagraph structure at all.

2. NO LOWER BOUND / INVENTED CEILING -- clean, and notably so. Both rows carry min null and max null. This is correct: §1344 contains no value, quantity, or dollar element as a trigger. The builder did not invent a ceiling and did not manufacture a floor.

3. PENALTY CAP TYPED AS TRIGGER -- correctly avoided, and this was the live trap in this section. The $1,000,000 figure is a fine ceiling in the flush penalty clause. Both rows leave max null and both trigger fields state explicitly that "The $1,000,000 figure is a fine ceiling, not a trigger threshold." That is the right call and the right reason.

4. CROSS-REFERENCES -- there are none to mis-map. The flush penalty clause attaches to the single "Whoever ... shall be" sentence covering both paragraphs; it names no paragraph, so no mapping error is possible, and the table's mapping (same penalty to both prongs) matches the operative words. The "or" joining (1) and (2) does make each prong an independent route, as both trigger fields say.

5. CARVE-OUTS -- I searched the fetched text: the string "except as provided" does not appear in §1344. The table's assertion on this point is verified true, not merely asserted.

6. LEVELS -- both rows level null. Correct; a Florida 921.0022 level on a federal section would be an error.

7. SCOPE -- both null. Correct; nothing in §1344 restricts application to a subset of conduct in a way a scope value would capture.

8. QUOTES -- I spot-checked both rows character by character against the fetched source. Every quoted run is verbatim, including the plain hyphen in "a scheme or artifice-" (the OLRC source really does use a hyphen there, not an em dash, so this is a faithful reproduction and not a normalization error), the serial comma in "assets, securities, or other property", the phrase "any of the moneys" (not "money"), and the penalty clause's unusual missing comma in "$1,000,000 or imprisoned". No splice: no heading is welded to body text, and no sentence is stopped mid-way without a marker.

COSMETIC NIT (does not affect any penalty datum, hence PASS): each row carries one ellipsis marker where nothing is actually elided. In row (1), the "..." between "artifice-" and "(1)" spans nothing -- paragraph (1) directly follows the intro clause in the source. In row (2), the "..." between "promises;" and "shall be fined" likewise spans nothing -- the flush penalty clause directly follows paragraph (2). Each row's other ellipsis is legitimate (row 1's elides paragraph (2); row 2's elides paragraph (1)). This is over-marking, the conservative direction: it can only suggest omitted text where there is none, never conceal omitted text, and it changes no term, bound, or element. Tightening would mean deleting the two spurious markers.

UNREAD FIELD -- honest, and I verified each of its three claims rather than accepting them. (a) The claim that the section has no lettered subsections and consists of intro + (1) + (2) + flush penalty is exactly what the raw HTML shows. (b) The claim that the 1989 amendment struck a former subsec. (b) defining "federally chartered or insured financial institution" is confirmed verbatim by the amendment note on the page. (c) The three externally-cited sections (18 U.S.C. 20, 3571, 3559) are correctly identified as outside §1344; §1344 does not cite any of them in its text, so declining to read them is a defensible boundary honestly disclosed rather than a gap concealed. readWhole true is warranted here on my own reading, not on the builder's say-so.

VERDICT BASIS -- complete on coverage (every provision that assigns a punishment is represented) and correct on the penalty data a page could repeat (term, bounds, fine-vs-trigger distinction, prong independence, absence of carve-outs). The only defect found is the pair of spurious ellipsis markers, which is cosmetic, so PASS with the nit recorded here.

1343.notes:
Independently fetched https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title18-section1343&num=0&edition=prelim (prelim text in effect Aug 13, 2026) and stripped it to plain text before opening the table.

STRUCTURE I BUILT MYSELF: Section 1343 is a single undesignated paragraph of exactly two sentences. There are no subsections, paragraphs, or subparagraphs. Punishment-assigning provisions: (1) first sentence, base offense, fine under this title or imprisonment not more than 20 years or both; (2) second sentence, which contains two independent disjunctive triggers sharing one penalty ("occurs in relation to ... a presidentially declared major disaster or emergency" OR "affects a financial institution"), fine not more than $1,000,000 or imprisonment not more than 30 years or both. That is three penalty provisions, and the table has exactly three rows. Nothing else in the granule assigns punishment: the only remaining material is the source credit and Editorial Notes/Amendments for 2008, 2002, 1994, 1990, 1989, 1956. The page's "Miscellaneous" jump link resolves to that Editorial Notes block; there is no Statutory Notes and Related Subsidiaries section, no effective-date note, no savings provision. Grep for "except as provided", "notwithstanding", proviso language, "effective", "short title": no hits in the section text. So the "no carve-out" claim in the unread field is verified, not merely asserted.

FAILURE-CLASS SWEEP:
1. No-lower-bound: correctly handled. Section 1343 states no dollar, quantity, or value element anywhere; all three rows carry min null and max null and say so explicitly. No invented floor.
2. Invented ceiling: none. No "or more" language exists to mis-cap.
3. Penalty cap typed as trigger: correctly avoided, and this is the trap this section sets. The $1,000,000 is a fine ceiling and appears only in trigger prose and quote, never in min/max. Same for the 20-year and 30-year terms.
4. Quote splice: I string-matched all three quotes against the fetched body. Row 1's quote is byte-exact and complete, no heading spliced on. Rows 2 and 3 quote the same single sentence from opposite ends; each fragment on either side of the ellipsis is verbatim, and both elisions are marked "...". Row 2 elides the disaster clause and the connecting "or"; row 3 elides "or affects a financial institution,". Neither elision changes meaning, since the two clauses are genuinely disjunctive and share one penalty.
5. Cross-references: "fined under this title" (to 3571), "financial institution" (to 18 U.S.C. 20), and "section 102 of the Stafford Act (42 U.S.C. 5122)" are all correctly identified as pointing outside the section and correctly disclosed as unread rather than guessed at. Nothing in the section cross-references back into its own conduct language, so there is no mis-mapping opportunity here. The second sentence's "such person" correctly refers back to "Whoever" in the first sentence, and the table treats it as an enhancement on the same conduct rather than a freestanding offense, which is right.
6. Levels: all three level fields are null, correct for a federal statute.
7. Scope: all null, not misused.
8. Unread field: honest and accurate. I verified the amendment-year list (2008, 2002, 1994, 1990, 1989, 1956) matches the page exactly, and readWhole:true is warranted.

Two non-defect observations, neither affecting verdict:
(a) "degree": "no degree assigned" is defensible. Section 1343 itself assigns no degree. 18 U.S.C. 3559 would classify the base offense as a Class C felony and the enhanced offense as a Class B felony by operation of their maximum terms, but that classification lives outside this section, so declining to import it is the conservative and correct call. It is arguably worth disclosing 3559 in the unread list alongside 3571 and 20, since it is a cross-reference of the same character that a reader might expect; this is a completeness-of-disclosure nicety, not an error in penalty data.
(b) Splitting one sentence into two rows is a modeling choice, not a defect. Both rows carry identical, correct penalties, and splitting makes each independent trigger visible rather than burying the financial-institution branch inside a disaster-titled row, which is the opposite of failure class 1.

I looked specifically for the mid-list omission this programme keeps catching and there is no list to hide in: the section is two sentences long and both are recorded. Coverage is whole-section and the penalty data is correct against the operative words.

wrong: 18 U.S.C. 2251(e), one-prior row and 2-or-more-prior row: both declare scope "prior" but leave min and max null, while the statute states the counts those tiers turn on -- "one prior conviction" and "2 or more prior convictions" (each appears exactly once in the fetched text). The row names the counted unit and then drops the number. If min/max carry the trigger threshold and scope names its unit (the schema's own vocabulary -- "prior" exists only for this purpose), the one-prior tier is min 1 / max 1 and the 2-or-more tier is min 2 / max NULL. The absent ceiling on "2 or more" is correct and must stay null on repair: the statute states no upper count, and writing 2 as a max on the one-prior row or inventing a ceiling on the 2+ row would be the 841(b)(1)(B) invented-ceiling error. This is the only place in section 2251 where a real numeric trigger exists, and it is the one place the table encoded nothing.

18 U.S.C. 2251(d)(1), scope "item": read literally, "item" asserts a threshold counted in items. The object of (d)(1) is a notice or advertisement, and the subsection states no count of notices, advertisements, or depictions -- one advertisement suffices. There is no item quantity in the text to scope to.

18 U.S.C. 2251(e), death-results row, scope "victim": the operative words are "engages in conduct that results in the death of a person" -- a result element, not a victim-count threshold, and "a person" is not limited to the minor. This row is also the only one of the four rows drawn from subsection (e)'s sentence block given a non-null scope; the base row, the attempt/conspiracy row, and the organization row are all null on identical facts (no counting element). The table is internally inconsistent about when scope is asserted.

18 U.S.C. 2251(a), (b), (c)(1): scope "victim", "victim", "place" asserted on rows whose own trigger text concedes there is no dollar, quantity, or count element. Defensible only if scope is a categorization field rather than the unit of min/max; under the literal reading these assert counting dimensions the statute does not supply. Lower confidence than the three findings above -- flagged for the schema owner, not asserted as a text error.
unread: Substance of the cross-referenced authorities named in subsection (e) -- 18 U.S.C. 1591, chapters 71, 109A, 117, chapter 110 generally, and the Uniform Code of Military Justice. Their citations inside (e) were verified verbatim against the fetched text; their contents are outside section 2251 and were not opened. This matches the builder's own disclosure.
2251.notes:
METHOD: curl-fetched the granule (214,965 bytes), stripped tags, normalized whitespace and dashes, and machine-tested every quote fragment for exact containment in the operative text with a binary-search break locator for any miss.

COVERAGE IS COMPLETE, and I verified that independently rather than accepting readWhole. Section 2251 contains exactly (a), (b), (c)(1), (c)(2)(A)-(B), (d)(1)(A)-(B), (d)(2)(A)-(B), (e). A regex sweep for subsection markers in the operative text returns only (a), (b), (c)(1), (d)(1), (e) plus the internal (e) cross-references; there is no (f). I also read the Editorial Notes and the Statutory Notes block in full -- Source Credit, Codification, Amendments, Short Title of 1978/1984/1986/1988/1990/1996/2006, Severability, Effective Date -- and none of it assigns a punishment, a mandatory minimum, or an enhancement. No provision lacks a row. completeness is set on my own walk of the section, not on the builder's claim.

WHAT I TESTED AND COULD NOT BREAK (stated so the parent does not re-audit these):
1. Quotes -- all 12 are verbatim, not 5 spot-checks. Every fragment matched exactly. Every elision is marked with "..." and none changes meaning. No inserted dash: the "is that- (A)" and "seeking or offering- (A)" joins in the (c)(2), (d)(2), and (d)(1) quotes reproduce a dash that is in the original text, flattened across a line break, not a heading spliced to a body.
2. Carve-outs -- the string "except" occurs zero times in the operative text. The (a) row's claim that no "except as provided in" clause appears anywhere in the section is true.
3. Cross-references -- all four conduct subsections route to subsection (e), and all four rows map them there: (a) "as provided under subsection (e)", (b) "subsection (e) of this section", (c)(1) "subsection (e)", (d)(1) "subsection (e)". Subsection (e) reaches back by "violates ... this section", so it covers all of (a)-(d). (c)(2) and (d)(2) are jurisdictional circumstance elements that assign no punishment, and the table says exactly that. No mis-mapping.
4. Terms -- 15/30, 25/50, 35/life, and death-or-not-less-than-30-or-life all match; each phrase occurs exactly once in the text.
5. The prior-conviction lists, which is where this section most invites error. The one-prior list does include section 1591 and the itemized child-pornography-conduct clause; the 2-or-more list does not, substituting "relating to the sexual exploitation of children". Confirmed by count: "section 1591" appears once in the section, while "chapter 71", "chapter 109A", "chapter 117", and "Uniform Code of Military Justice" each appear twice. The table's note calling out this asymmetry is correct.
6. No fine cap typed as a trigger (the 924(p) error) -- "fined under this title" is nowhere in min/max. No invented ceiling -- "life" and "2 or more" both left unbounded. All levels null, correct for a federal statute. All degrees "no degree assigned", correct.
7. The builder's unread field is honest. Its three entries are accurate: the operative subsections were in fact all read, the editorial matter it declines is in fact non-operative, and its disclosure about the cross-referenced chapters is candid. No false claim there.

WHY FAIL AND NOT PASS: the defects are confined to the structured scope/min/max layer, but the rubric lists a misused scope as FAIL-worthy, and the prior-conviction finding is not a formatting nit -- it is a numeric trigger the statute states and the row leaves null while simultaneously declaring the unit it counts. A downstream page would render two enhancement tiers with no machine-readable count, and any later attempt to fill them risks writing a ceiling the statute does not state.

COSMETIC ONLY, not verdict-bearing: (i) two rows both cite "18 U.S.C. 2251(e)" for the base individual penalty -- the second (attempt/conspiracy) adds no distinct range and quotes the same sentence, so it is a duplicate rather than a separate provision; (ii) cite-labeling is inconsistent -- (c)(2)(A),(B) and (d)(2)(A),(B) get named subparagraph cites but (d)(1)(A),(B) do not, though both subparagraphs were genuinely read and described in that row's trigger, so this is not a coverage gap.

missing: (f) — the section-wide CARVE-OUT. 'This section does not prohibit any lawfully authorized investigative, protective, or intelligence activity of a law enforcement agency of the United States, a State, or a political subdivision of a State, or of an intelligence agency of the United States.' No row, and no row anywhere mentions it. This is the one exemption that defeats every (a) paragraph and therefore every (c) tier in the table. Failure class 5 exactly.

(j), and its paragraphs (j)(1) and (j)(2) — a forfeiture provision with no row. '(j) For purposes of subsection (i), the following shall be subject to forfeiture to the United States and no property right shall exist in them: (1) Any personal property used or intended to be used to commit or to facilitate the commission of any violation of this section, or a conspiracy to violate this section. (2) Any property, real or personal, which constitutes or is derived from proceeds traceable to any violation of this section, or a conspiracy to violate this section'. The table mentions (j) only inside the (i)(1) trigger prose; a mention in another row's prose is not a row. Note (j)(2) reaches property 'derived from proceeds TRACEABLE to' a violation, which is broader than (i)(1)(B)'s 'proceeds that such person obtained, directly or indirectly'.

(i)(2) — no row. Governs the criminal forfeiture procedure by 21 U.S.C. 853 'except subsection (d) of that section'. The (d) exclusion (the rebuttable presumption of forfeitability) is a substantive limit on the forfeiture penalty; it survives only as a clause in the (i)(1) trigger prose.

(g) — the civil remedy provision, no row. It fixes who may sue, caps damages to economic damages where the conduct is (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) only, restricts suit to conduct involving subclauses (I) through (V) of (c)(4)(A)(i) (thereby EXCLUDING the (VI) 10-computer branch entirely), and imposes a 2-year limitations period. The table's (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) row leans on (g) but (g) itself has no row and the (VI) exclusion is stated nowhere.

(a)(5)(A), (a)(5)(B) and (a)(5)(C) — no element rows, although the table gave element rows to (a)(4) and (a)(7). Every tier in (c)(4) is a cross-reference into these three subparagraphs, so the conduct text the whole of (c)(4) maps onto is absent from the table. (a)(5)(C) is the sharpest gap: it is the only (a)(5) branch whose bare first offence falls to the 1-year (c)(4)(G) catch-all, and its text carries footnote 2 ('So in original. The period probably should be a semicolon.').
(a)(1) — no element row, although (c)(1)(A) and (c)(1)(B) exist only to punish it.

(a)(2), and its subparagraphs (A), (B), (C) — no element rows, although (c)(2)(A), (c)(2)(B) and (c)(2)(C) all map onto it. (a)(2)(C) 'information from any protected computer' is what makes the 5-year (c)(2)(B) tier reach ordinary private-sector data.
(a)(3) — no element row, though punished by (c)(2)(A) and (c)(2)(C).
(a)(6), and its subparagraphs (A) and (B) — no element rows, though punished by (c)(2)(A) and (c)(2)(C). (a)(6)(B) carries footnote 3 ('So in original. Probably should be followed by "or".').
(c) chapeau — 'The punishment for an offense under subsection (a) or (b) of this section is-'. No row. It is the operative sentence that converts every (a) and (b) offence into a (c) penalty.
wrong: MISUSED scope, and the most material defect: scope 'prior' is set on five rows that are expressly the NON-recidivist tiers. (c)(1)(A), (c)(2)(A), (c)(3)(A), (c)(4)(A)(i) and (c)(4)(B)(i) each read 'which does NOT occur after a conviction for another offense under this section'. Read literally — as the audit requires scope be read — 'prior' asserts these rows are keyed to a prior conviction, inverting the tier. A page repeating this would present the 10-year first-offence tier for (a)(1) as the repeat tier, and would leave the actual 20-year repeat tier (c)(1)(B) indistinguishable from it. The trigger prose says the opposite of the scope value on the same row, so one of the two is wrong on its face.

MISUSED scope on (c)(4)(A)(i)(I): scope 'victim' with min 5000. The statute expressly AGGREGATES: 'loss to 1 or more persons during any 1-year period (and, for purposes of an investigation, prosecution, or other proceeding brought by the United States only, loss resulting from a related course of conduct affecting 1 or more other protected computers) aggregating at least $5,000 in value'. Read literally, scope 'victim' makes $5,000 a per-victim floor. It is a single aggregate floor summed across all persons and, in a United States proceeding, across related conduct on other computers. The row's own trigger prose states the aggregation and then contradicts it with the scope value.

MISUSED scope on (a)(4): scope 'item' on a row with min null and max null and no item-count element anywhere in (a)(4). The only figure in the paragraph is the $5,000 use-only carve-out, which the row itself correctly says is not a threshold. 'item' asserts a per-item measurement that the paragraph does not contain.

MISUSED scope on (i)(1): scope 'item' on the forfeiture row. Forfeiture under (i)(1) has no threshold and no per-item measurement — (A) reaches the person's interest in any personal property used or intended to be used, (B) reaches any property constituting or derived from proceeds. There is nothing for 'item' to scope.

scope asserted on rows that have no threshold to scope: 'victim' on (c)(4)(A)(i)(II), (c)(4)(A)(i)(III), (c)(4)(E) and (c)(4)(F); 'item' on (c)(4)(A)(i)(V). All five have min null and max null. Where the field is a measurement unit for min/max, populating it on a null-bounded row is a literal misuse, and it is inconsistent with the table's own practice of leaving scope null on the other null-bounded rows ((a)(7), (b), (c)(2)(B), (c)(2)(B)(i), (c)(2)(B)(ii), (c)(4)(A)(ii), and so on).

Internally inconsistent scope on the two $5,000 rows: (c)(2)(B)(iii) has min 5000 with scope null, while (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) has min 5000 with scope 'victim'. The two figures are measured differently — (c)(2)(B)(iii) is the value of the information obtained, (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) is aggregated loss — but the table's scope field does not distinguish them; it leaves one blank and mislabels the other.

(c)(4)(A)(i)(I) trigger prose overstates (g): 'is the only branch that supports a civil action limited to economic damages under (g)'. (g) permits a civil action on ANY of subclauses (I) through (V); what is unique to (I) is only the economic-damages CAP where the conduct involves (I) alone. The sentence as written reads as though (I) were the only civil-action branch. The prose also omits the operative consequence for the row directly below it: subclause (VI), the 10-or-more-computers branch, supports no civil action at all under (g).

'unread' is not honest. It lists two note groups that DO NOT EXIST in this section — there is no 'Effective Date of 1996, 1994 and 1986 Amendments' note and no 'Short Title' note under 18 U.S.C. 1030; the only Effective Date note is the 2002 one, which is listed separately. Conversely it OMITS a note that does exist: 'Transfer of Functions' (transfer of the Secret Service and the Secretary of the Treasury's related functions to the Secretary of Homeland Security), which bears directly on (d)(1) and (d)(3), both of which name the Secret Service and the Secretary of the Treasury. Padding the list with invented entries while dropping a real one makes the field unusable as a coverage record.

1030.notes:
METHOD: fetched the OLRC page with curl and stripped it to text before opening the table; built an independent list of every punishment-, minimum-, and enhancement-assigning provision, then compared.

WHAT THE TABLE GOT RIGHT (verified against the fetched text, stated so the parent does not re-litigate it): every cross-reference from (c) back into (a) is correctly mapped — (c)(1) to (a)(1); (c)(2)(A) and (c)(2)(C) to (a)(2),(a)(3),(a)(6); (c)(2)(B) to (a)(2) ALONE; (c)(3) to (a)(4),(a)(7); (c)(4)(A)(i) to (a)(5)(B); (c)(4)(B)(i) to (a)(5)(A); (c)(4)(C)(i) to (a)(5)(A) and (a)(5)(B); (c)(4)(D)(i) to (a)(5)(C); (c)(4)(E) and (F) to (a)(5)(A); (c)(4)(G)(i) to any other (a)(5) offence. Every term of years matches the text (10/20; 1/5/10; 5/10; 5/10/20/10/20/life/1). No INVENTED CEILING anywhere — every max is null, including on (c)(2)(B)(iii) ('exceeds $5,000', correctly not capped at any next tier) and (c)(4)(A)(i)(VI) ('10 or more'). No PENALTY CAP typed as a trigger — 'a fine under this title' is nowhere written into min or max. All levels are null, correct for a federal statute. The two inclusivity calls are right: 'at least $5,000' inclusive, 'exceeds $5,000' exclusive. The 'except as provided in subparagraphs (E) and (F)' carve-out is caught on (A), (B) and (C), and its ABSENCE from (D) is correctly flagged. The (c)(4)(G) catch-all — the row this audit expected to be missing — is present.

QUOTES: I spot-checked well past five — (a)(4), (a)(7), (b), (c)(1)(A), (c)(1)(B), (c)(2)(A), (c)(2)(B), (c)(2)(C), (c)(3)(A), (c)(3)(B), (c)(4)(A)(i), (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) through (VI), (c)(4)(B) through (G), (i)(1) — against the fetched text. All verbatim. No splice: every chapeau-to-clause join ((a)(7), (c)(4)(A)/(B)/(C)/(D)/(G), (i)(1)) is contiguous statutory text needing no ellipsis, and the one true elision, in (c)(2)(B) where clauses (i) and (ii) are dropped, is marked '...'. The OLRC page itself renders the em dashes as plain hyphens, so the table's 'if-' and 'obtains-' reproduce the source rather than inserting a dash. Footnote 4 on (c)(3)(B) is quoted accurately. Dropping the superscript footnote markers (2, 3, 4) from quoted text is normal practice, not an alteration.

WHY FAIL RATHER THAN PASS: correctness fails on the scope axis, which the materiality rule names explicitly. The scope 'prior' error is not cosmetic — it is set on five rows and it says the opposite of what those five rows' operative words say, and it is the kind of field a downstream page prints as a recidivism label. The scope 'victim' on (c)(4)(A)(i)(I) converts an expressly aggregated $5,000 floor into a per-victim one, which changes who is chargeable at the 5-year and 10-year tiers.

WHY completeness IS 'partial' AND NOT 'whole-section': the criminal-penalty spine of (c) is genuinely complete, and I confirmed there is no (c)(5) (struck by Pub. L. 110-326, §204(a)(2)(D) in 2008), so the table is right that (c)(4)(G)(ii) closes the subsection. But completeness is coverage of the section, not of subsection (c). Forfeiture is a punishment: (i)(1) has a row while (i)(2) and all of (j) have none. Subsection (f) is an exemption from the entire section and appears nowhere. And the table set the precedent of writing element rows for conduct paragraphs by writing them for (a)(4) and (a)(7), then omitted the other five — including all three (a)(5) subparagraphs, which are the referents of the eleven (c)(4) rows that make up a third of the table.
